steps.player: What's the supercompost potion for?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Oh, let one see peasant - perhaps it is a potion for making supercompost?

steps.player: No, I didn't mean that-

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: You wish to know how to use it? Pour it on some normal compost and it will transform into supercompost. You can do this with a bucket of compost, although it is possibly wiser to use it on a full compost bin.

options.text: Can I use this garden for my own farming?

steps.player: Can I use this garden for my own farming?

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: What, you want to dig up the plants that took one so long to grow? Don't be ridiculous, you silly little fool.

steps.player: All right then, sorry I asked.

steps.speaker: Queen Ellamaria
steps.text: Impertinent peasant! Oh, if you promise to leave one alone then feel free to pick fruit from the White Tree. One is told that they are a great natural energy restorative.

options.text: Is there anything I can do for you?

jump-4e84b779d3b37829.text: If the player is in a F2P world:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Thanks, but I don't have anything I need doing right now.

jump-4e84b779d3b37829.text: If the player is in a members world:

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: What did you ask me to do?

steps.text: Continues to his tasks

options.text: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

steps.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

options.text: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.player: I'd just like to ask you something.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Please do!

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Yes please.
Thanks, maybe some other time.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.
If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about what's underground.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh, the dwarven realms?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: incinerate you where you stand.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.player: What does poison do?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What monsters drop good items?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about valiant heroes!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ha ha ha... There are plenty of heroes. Always have been, always will be, until the fall of the world.
If the player has less than 80 quest points:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you'd do a few more quests, you'd soon become a fairly noted adventurer yourself.
If the player has 80 or more quest points:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You're quite a noted adventurer yourself!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But I suppose I could tell you of a couple...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, there was a man called Arrav. No-one knew where he came from, but he was a fearsome fighter, a skillful hunter and a remarkable farmer. He lived in the ancient settlement of Avarrocka, defending it from

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: goblins, until he went forth in search of some strange artefact long desired by the dreaded Mahjarrat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps some day I shall be able to tell you what became of him.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But do not let your head be turned by heroics. Randas was another great man, but he let himself be beguiled into turning to serve Zamorak, and they say he is now a mindless creature deep in the Underground Pass that

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: leads to Isafdar.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Where did humans learn to use magic?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, that was quite a discovery! It revolutionised our way of life and jolted us into this Fifth Age of the world.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: They say a traveller in the north discovered the key, although no records state exactly what he found. From this he was able to summon the magic of the four elements, using magic as a tool and a weapon. He and

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: his followers learnt how to bind the power into little stones so that others could use it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: in the land south of here they constructed an immense tower where the power could be studied, but followers of Zamorak destroyed it with fire many years ago, and most of the knowledge was lost.
If the player hasn't completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps one day those lost secrets will be uncovered once more.
If the player has completed Rune Mysteries:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I hear you've been very helpful to the wizards who are working on the mysteries of the rune stones.

steps.player: Well, I didn't do much...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I suppose you'd know about the history of today's cities?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, there are fairly good records of the formation of the cities from primitive settlements.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: In the early part of the Fourth Age, of course, there were no permanent settlements. Tribes wandered the lands, staying where they could until the resources were exhausted.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: This changed as people learnt to grow crops and breed animals, and now there are very few of the old nomadic tribes. There's at least one tribe roaming between the Troll Stronghold and Rellekka, though.
If the player has completed Mountain Daughter:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them. They're all mad.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Truly, their faith in natural spirits is rather foolish, but they're a pleasant enough people.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Anyway, what was I saying? Ah, yes...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: One settlement was Avarrocka, a popular trading centre.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: In the west, Ardougne gradually formed under the leadership of the Carnillean family, despite the threat of the Mahjarrat warlord Hazeel who dwelt in that area until his downfall.
If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: He'll be back, just you wait!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh dear, I hope you haven't done anything rash!
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: The Wise Old Man of Draynor Village

steps.player: Tell me about yourself, old man.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, so you want to know about me, eh?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Mmm... what could I say about myself? Let's see what I've done...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've delved into the dungeon west of Brimhaven and heard the terrifying CRASH of the steel dragons battling each other for territory.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I spent some years on Entrana, where I learnt the techniques of pure meditation.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've wandered through the vast desert that lies south of Al Kharid and seen the great walls of Menaphos and Sophanem.
If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper:

steps.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

steps.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!

steps.player: But I've met the Sph...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Even if such a creature were to exist...

steps.player: ... which it does...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!

steps.player: Hmmm?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Apart from all that, I've spent many a happy hour in dusty libraries, searching through ancient scrolls and texts for the wisdom of those who have passed on.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Plus plenty of other adventures, quests, journeys... Is there anything else you'd like to know?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Zamorak craves only death and destruction.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.
If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.player: So who's Zaros?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.

steps.player: So Zaros is real?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!
If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?

steps.player: Um... Yes, I suppose so.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.
(If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.
(If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.
If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?

steps.player: Umm...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!

steps.player: But...?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I know what I know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.

steps.player: How did it all end?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are the Mahjarrat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.
If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've defeated Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.
If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.
If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.
If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh dear, oh dear...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You've seen the bank's security recording?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That's my plan, yes.

steps.player: But that's... well, it's WRONG!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Bah!

steps.player: Hmmph!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.

steps.player: Can I buy your hat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I think I'll keep it.

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?

steps.player: Go on...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.

steps.player: But you're retired!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

jump-36063ba2c6b795d2.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-36063ba2c6b795d2.text: Ha ha! I thought you might try that!! But remember, [player name] - the power of the Ring of Charos will not work with everybody, especially not a wise old bird like me!

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Yes please.
Thanks, maybe some other time.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.
If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about what's underground.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh, the dwarven realms?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: incinerate you where you stand.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.player: What does poison do?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What monsters drop good items?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Zamorak craves only death and destruction.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.
If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.player: So who's Zaros?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.

steps.player: So Zaros is real?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!
If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?

steps.player: Um... Yes, I suppose so.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.
(If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.
(If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.
If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?

steps.player: Umm...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!

steps.player: But...?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I know what I know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.

steps.player: How did it all end?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are the Mahjarrat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.
If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've defeated Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.
If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.
If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.
If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh dear, oh dear...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You've seen the bank's security recording?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That's my plan, yes.

steps.player: But that's... well, it's WRONG!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Bah!

steps.player: Hmmph!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.

steps.player: Can I buy your hat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I think I'll keep it.

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?

steps.player: Go on...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.

steps.player: But you're retired!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

jump-674188d3aea50e4f.text: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.

jump-9ee0a940eb75b54f.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

jump-d2e40c9732629a29.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-d2e40c9732629a29.text: If everything I have heard about Charos's ring is true, it will not stay lost forever. Where did you originally find it?

jump-d2e40c9732629a29.player: I ... um ... 'borrowed' it from a rather shady character called Fenkenstrain.

jump-d2e40c9732629a29.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-d2e40c9732629a29.text: In order to find the ring it may be wise to return to Fenkenstrain - he may have found a way to regain it. If you manage to reobtain the ring, return to me and I will reveal its secrets to you.

jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.text: Lost the Ring of Charos?!? That is indeed a disastrous turn of events. This ring that you have so casually thrown away possesses hidden power beyond belief.

jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.player: How can I re-obtain the Ring of Charos?

jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.text: If everything I have heard about Charos's ring is true, it will not stay lost forever. Where did you originally find it?

jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.player: I ... um ... 'borrowed' it from a rather shady character called Fenkenstrain.

jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-581c4f5573c5dd7d.text: In order to find the ring it may be wise to return to Fenkenstrain - he may have found a way to regain it. If you manage to reobtain the ring, return to me and I will reveal its secrets to you.

jump-f242aaf282f8e8c8.player: I think you wanted to give me a thousand coins...

jump-f242aaf282f8e8c8.speaker: Wise Old Man
jump-f242aaf282f8e8c8.text: Ha ha! I thought you might try that!! But remember, [player name] - the power of the Ring of Charos will not work with everybody, especially not a wise old bird like me!

iXrXau.speaker: Wise Old Man
iXrXau.text: Thanks, but I don't have anything I need doing right now.

shjW_t.player: Could you check my items for junk, please?

shjW_t.text: (Game opens the Wise Old Man's Recycling Center interface)

Ds2B1E.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

Ds2B1E.speaker: Wise Old Man
Ds2B1E.text: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

Ds2B1E.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

dsGd7p.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

dsGd7p.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Even if such a creature were to exist...

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...

0keLec.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

0keLec.speaker: Wise Old Man
0keLec.text: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!

8-MPbm.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

8-MPbm.speaker: Wise Old Man
8-MPbm.text: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.

iPpubb.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

iPpubb.speaker: Wise Old Man
iPpubb.text: Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.
